function.name: search_cryptos

Such a hit looks like a normal success - one or two rows, no error, and no similarity or confidence field, so the returned name, symbol and rank are the only signal of match quality.

One term per call: "BTC,ETH" and "BTC ETH" return an empty array. No match also returns an empty array, not an error.

One row comes back as an array of objects; two or more as {headers, rows}, where each row's values follow the order in headers.

limit.description: Max rows, default 3, valid 1-5. Raising it does not surface more candidates - matching returns 0-2 rows either way.

query.description: One coin's name, symbol or slug, case-insensitive: "BTC", "btc", "Bitcoin", "bitcoin". A multi-word coin name like "Bitcoin Cash" is fine; a list of coins is not.

function.name: get_crypto_quotes_latest

0 or 1 matches return an array of objects; 2 or more return {headers, rows}. Header order varies between calls, so a column index learned from one call will not hold in the next. Rows come back in the order the ids were given, and id comes back as a string. Each row is roughly 650 characters.

isError stays false when nothing is found: an unknown id is dropped silently, so a 5-id call can return 4 rows or an empty array, and inactive coins come back with null price and rank. Missing or null is no data, not a price of zero.

id.description: One or more CoinMarketCap numeric ids as one comma-separated string with no whitespace: "1" or "1,1027" (Bitcoin is 1). id.description: Exactly one CoinMarketCap numeric id, digits only, e.g. "1" (Bitcoin), with no whitespace. A symbol, a slug or a comma-separated list all fail with "id is not number", so query several coins with one call each. Numeric ids come from search_cryptos.

includeFields.description:

function.name: get_crypto_latest_news

Asset matching is loose and items carry no id or symbol field, so an item can be about a different asset or not recent, with the title as the only relevance signal.

id.description: Exactly one CoinMarketCap numeric id, digits only, e.g. "1" (Bitcoin). A symbol fails with "id is not number"; a well-formed but unknown id returns an empty list, not an error. Numeric ids come from search_cryptos.

function.name: trending_crypto_narratives
function.description:

Takes no parameters: a named narrative cannot be requested, and there is no limit, sort or filter argument.

The response carries no news content and no social posts, sentiment or engagement metrics. Its only social fields are socialKeywords, a list of raw keyword strings, and socialKeywordUniqueAuthorCount.

Returns categoryList as a headers plus positional rows table, whose topCoinList column nests a second headers/rows table carrying a few coins with a 7d price change each; it does not identify a narrative's constituent tokens. slug identifies a narrative, ranks are positions within this response, and the same slug can appear more than once. Every figure is a display string, not a number ("1.64 T", "+6.67%").

Repeated calls can return an identical cached snapshot.

function.name: get_upcoming_macro_events
function.description:
Forward-dated crypto catalysts extracted from news articles - a news-derived catalyst list, not an authoritative economic calendar. Because dates are read out of article text, a dated claim inside an article, such as an analyst target or a prediction-market quote, can surface as a row with the same shape as a scheduled event; the row does not distinguish the two. Which event types are present at any time follows the upstream news corpus, so a type absent from the response reflects the corpus, not the absence of a scheduled event.

Returns one key upcomingEventNews as headers plus positional rows: title, content, url, eventDate, originalNewsContent. Row order is unsorted and changes between calls, so the first row is not the nearest event, and one event can occupy several rows sourced from different sites.

content is a snippet hard-cut at 100 characters, often mid-word. The full text, and the country or jurisdiction an event belongs to, appear only in originalNewsContent. eventDate is a display string - for example "10 August 2026", sometimes with a time and UTC offset - not ISO-8601.

One call returns tens of KB, most of it source-article text, and cannot be narrowed: no parameters, no date, type or region filter, no way to change the row count.

function.name: propose_trade

action.description: LONG or SHORT to open risk, HOLD to do nothing, CLOSE to exit.

confidence.description: Your probability (0.0 to 1.0) that your directional view is correct. For LONG/SHORT: that price moves in the trade's favor over the time horizon. entry_price.description: Required for LONG/SHORT: the current price from get_price. Omit if you have no price.

evidence.description: Every fact your decision relies on.

source_tool.description: Name of the tool that returned this fact.

value.description: The number exactly as it appears in the tool result, same units. Omit this field when the claim has no number, e.g. a tool returned an error. Never write 0 as a stand-in.

No paging, offset, date, language or source filter; limit can only shrink the list.

id.description: Exactly one CoinMarketCap numeric id, digits only, e.g. "1" (Bitcoin). A symbol fails with "id is not number"; a well-formed but unknown id returns an empty list, not an error. Numeric ids come from search_cryptos.

limit.description: Requested item count, default 10. The response never exceeds 10 items, so a larger value does not widen coverage; 0 or a negative value is ignored and the default applies.

function.name: trending_crypto_narratives
function.description:
A ranked snapshot of which CoinMarketCap narrative categories are trending, with each one's aggregate market cap, volume and percent change over 24h, 7d, 30d, 90d and 1y, plus performance relative to the whole crypto market.

Takes no parameters: a named narrative cannot be requested, and there is no limit, sort or filter argument.

The response carries no news content and no social posts, sentiment or engagement metrics. Its only social fields are socialKeywords, a list of raw keyword strings, and socialKeywordUniqueAuthorCount.

Returns categoryList as a headers plus positional rows table, whose topCoinList column nests a second headers/rows table carrying a few coins with a 7d price change each; it does not identify a narrative's constituent tokens. slug identifies a narrative, ranks are positions within this response, and the same slug can appear more than once. Every figure is a display string, not a number ("1.64 T", "+6.67%").

Repeated calls can return an identical cached snapshot.

function.name: get_upcoming_macro_events
function.description:
Forward-dated crypto catalysts extracted from news articles - a news-derived catalyst list, not an authoritative economic calendar. Because dates are read out of article text, a dated claim inside an article, such as an analyst target or a prediction-market quote, can surface as a row with the same shape as a scheduled event; the row does not distinguish the two. Which event types are present at any time follows the upstream news corpus, so a type absent from the response reflects the corpus, not the absence of a scheduled event.

Returns one key upcomingEventNews as headers plus positional rows: title, content, url, eventDate, originalNewsContent. Row order is unsorted and changes between calls, so the first row is not the nearest event, and one event can occupy several rows sourced from different sites.

content is a snippet hard-cut at 100 characters, often mid-word. The full text, and the country or jurisdiction an event belongs to, appear only in originalNewsContent. eventDate is a display string - for example "10 August 2026", sometimes with a time and UTC offset - not ISO-8601.

One call returns tens of KB, most of it source-article text, and cannot be narrowed: no parameters, no date, type or region filter, no way to change the row count.

function.name: propose_trade
function.description: Submit your final trading decision. Call this exactly once, as your last step. It is a proposal only: a deterministic risk governor will approve, resize, or reject it.

action.description: LONG or SHORT to open risk, HOLD to do nothing, CLOSE to exit.

confidence.description: Your probability (0.0 to 1.0) that your directional view is correct. For LONG/SHORT: that price moves in the trade's favor over the time horizon. For HOLD/CLOSE: your strongest conviction in either direction; if you are holding because the signal is unclear or data is missing, this should be low.

position_size_pct.description: Fraction of account equity, e.g. 0.03 means 3%. Use 0 for HOLD.

entry_price.description: Required for LONG/SHORT: the current price from get_price. Omit if you have no price.

evidence.description: Every fact your decision relies on.

source_tool.description: Name of the tool that returned this fact.

value.description: The number exactly as it appears in the tool result, same units. Omit this field when the claim has no number, e.g. a tool returned an error. Never write 0 as a stand-in.

trajectory.prompt: If Bitcoin's market dominance is above 58.7% right now, go long BTC; otherwise short BTC.

market_size.definition: Market size captures the aggregate USD value of the entire crypto asset class, providing a top-down gauge of how large or small the market is relative to history or to other cryptos or asset classes.

liquidity.definition: Liquidity metrics track how much value changes hands—across spot markets and derivatives—within 24 h, signalling market depth, conviction, and the ease of entering or exiting positions.

fear_greed.definition: The CMC Fear & Greed Index distills overall crypto-market sentiment into a single 0-100 score that traders can read contrarily—treating high, greed-driven readings (overvalued) as cues to trim or hedge, low, fear-driven readings (undervalued) as potential bargain zones.

altcoin_season.definition: The CMC Altcoin Season Index is a real-time sentiment gauge of crypto’s typical rotation—Bitcoin rallies and dominance rise, Ethereum heats up on dApp buzz, narratives catch fire, then capital floods into smaller alts—so a rising score signals the shift toward higher-beta altcoins, while a falling score warns funds are moving back to Bitcoin or cash.

dominance.definition: Bitcoin dominance—BTC’s share of total crypto value—condenses sentiment, maturity, and diversification cues: rising dominance favors a defensive tilt into Bitcoin, while falling dominance signals a risk-on swing toward altcoins.

leverage.definition: Leverage fields measure borrowed-risk exposure via derivatives open interest, funding rates, and liquidations, revealing how much speculative fuel—or squeeze risk—is in the system.

trad_fi_flows.definition: TradFi flows capture capital moving into or out of regulated exchange-traded products—such as U.S. spot-BTC ETFs—acting as a proxy for institutional demand.

function.name: search_cryptos
function.description:
Resolve one cryptocurrency name, symbol or slug to the CoinMarketCap numeric id that asset-scoped tools take as input. Returns id, name, symbol, slug and rank - no price data.

Matching is near-exact on one term, not fuzzy and not ranked by market cap. A partial or misspelled term matches literally and can miss the major coin: "bit" returns BitDAO and Biconomy, not Bitcoin; "bitcon" returns BitCone. Such a hit looks like a normal success - one or two rows, no error, and no similarity or confidence field, so the returned name, symbol and rank are the only signal of match quality.

One term per call: "BTC,ETH" and "BTC ETH" return an empty array. No match also returns an empty array, not an error.

One row comes back as an array of objects; two or more as {headers, rows}, where each row's values follow the order in headers.

limit.description: Max rows, default 3, valid 1-5. Raising it does not surface more candidates - matching returns 0-2 rows either way.

query.description: One coin's name, symbol or slug, case-insensitive: "BTC", "btc", "Bitcoin", "bitcoin". A multi-word coin name like "Bitcoin Cash" is fine; a list of coins is not.

function.name: get_crypto_quotes_latest
function.description:
Current market quote for one or more cryptocurrencies - the default tool for price questions. USD only, current snapshot only: no history, no top-N or biggest-mover list.

Returns 36 snake_case fields per coin, including price, market_cap, market_cap_dominance, volume_24h, volume_change_24h, fully_diluted_market_cap, circulating_supply, total_supply, max_supply, turnover, rank, date_added and last_updated_time. percent_change_ covers 1h, 24h, 7d, 30d, 60d, 90d, ytd, 1y and all; market_cap_percent_change_ covers the same periods except 60d and ytd.

0 or 1 matches return an array of objects; 2 or more return {headers, rows}. Header order varies between calls, so a column index learned from one call will not hold in the next. Rows come back in the order the ids were given, and id comes back as a string. Each row is roughly 650 characters.

isError stays false when nothing is found: an unknown id is dropped silently, so a 5-id call can return 4 rows or an empty array, and inactive coins come back with null price and rank. Missing or null is no data, not a price of zero.

id.description: One or more CoinMarketCap numeric ids as one comma-separated string with no whitespace: "1" or "1,1027" (Bitcoin is 1). Digits only, and one string rather than an array - symbols, slugs, decimals ("BTC", "bitcoin", "1.5") and a space after a comma ("1, 1027") all fail with an opaque server error that names no cause. Numeric ids come from search_cryptos.

function.name: get_crypto_technical_analysis
function.description:
Price technical analysis for ONE cryptocurrency. Returns five blocks, whose keys are also the includeFields values: moving_averages (SMA and EMA, fixed 7/30/200-day), macd, rsi (fixed 7/14/21), fibonacciLevels (retracement and extension), pivotPoint.

Windows are fixed - no interval, period or lookback parameter. Every value is a display string, not a number ("63,612.69"). The response echoes no id, name or symbol.

Whole-market technical analysis is a different tool, get_crypto_marketcap_technical_analysis.

id.description: Exactly one CoinMarketCap numeric id, digits only, e.g. "1" (Bitcoin), with no whitespace. A symbol, a slug or a comma-separated list all fail with "id is not number", so query several coins with one call each. Numeric ids come from search_cryptos.

includeFields.description:
Optional array selecting whole blocks from the five above. Values are case-sensitive and must match the response keys exactly: "moving_averages", "macd", "rsi", "fibonacciLevels", "pivotPoint" - not indicator spellings like "SMA", "Fibonacci" or "pivot points", and not nested keys like "rsi14". It only filters; it cannot add fields absent from the default response.

Omit it or pass [] to get all five. Unrecognized values are dropped one by one with no error, so an all-invalid filter returns {} with isError false - a bad filter value, not a coin without technical analysis.

function.name: get_crypto_marketcap_technical_analysis
function.description:
Technical analysis of the TOTAL crypto market capitalization - the whole market, not any single coin. Single-coin technical analysis is a different tool, get_crypto_technical_analysis.

Takes no parameters. An id, or any other argument, is silently ignored and the response is identical, so a normal response is never proof the data was scoped to a coin.

Returns macd; rsi with fixed 7/14/21 windows and no timeframe option; fibonacciLevels (swingHigh, swingLow, retracementLevels, extensionLevels - none of them labeled support or resistance); pivotPoint, on a market-cap basis, not a price; and currentMarketCap plus currentVolume, the whole-market totals. No moving averages. Every value is a display string, not a number: market-cap, volume, MACD and fibonacci figures carry a T/B/M magnitude suffix ("2.15 T"), rsi values do not ("40.15").

function.name: get_global_metrics_latest
function.description:
Whole-crypto-market snapshot, USD only, no parameters. Returns one fixed ~5.5 KB dashboard with 8 sections: last_updated, market_size (total market cap), liquidity (24h volume - total, spot, derivatives, plus a spot_vs_perp_ratio), sentiment (fear and greed), rotation (altcoin season), dominance (btc, eth, others), leverage (open interest, average funding rate, and BTC-only liquidation totals with no long/short split), and trad_fi_flows (BTC and ETH spot-ETF AUM). Windows come from a fixed vocabulary - 24h/7d/30d change, yesterday/last_week/ last_month history, yearly max/min - and not every section carries all of them.

ETF data is AUM levels only; net inflow or outflow is absent, and AUM differences are not flows.

Every value is a display string, not a number - T/B/M suffixes and +/- glyphs ("2.15 T", "389.54 B", "+58.4%"), timestamps as rendered text ("3 August 2026 12:00 AM UTC+0"). Dominance carries a leading + but is a share of total market cap, not a change. The fear-and-greed and altcoin-season index integers are the only numeric fields, and the altcoin-season regime is delivered as that index on a 0-100 scale. About 1.4 KB of the payload is definition prose.

Freshness is mixed: open interest, market-cap changes, volume and dominance move intraday, while fear and greed, altcoin season and ETF AUM come from a daily 00:00 UTC snapshot. last_updated is that daily label, not the as-of time of the intraday fields.

There is no asset, convert-currency or window parameter: the reply is always this same whole-market USD payload.

function.name: get_global_crypto_derivatives_metrics
function.description:
Global crypto derivatives snapshot, no arguments: open interest and volume for total, futures and perpetuals, each with 24h, 7d, 14d and 30d change windows; one blended funding rate with the same windows; and BTC liquidations by 1h, 4h, 12h and 24h window split long versus short.

Values are live intraday and the payload carries no timestamp of any kind, so figures cannot be given an as-of time. Every value is a display string, not a number ("385.08 B", "993,927.14").

Boundaries: funding is one global blended rate, unit not marked in the value and averaging method undisclosed - no per-exchange or per-contract funding. Liquidations are BTC only. No long/short open-interest ratio and no positioning data, so leverage imbalance is not a field here; no options, basis or implied volatility; no history beyond the fixed change windows.

There is no symbol, exchange or interval parameter; the same fixed snapshot comes back regardless.

function.name: search_cryptos
function.description:
Resolve one cryptocurrency name, symbol or slug to the CoinMarketCap numeric id that asset-scoped tools take as input. Returns id, name, symbol, slug and rank - no price data.

Matching is near-exact on one term, not fuzzy and not ranked by market cap. A partial or misspelled term matches literally and can miss the major coin: "bit" returns BitDAO and Biconomy, not Bitcoin; "bitcon" returns BitCone. Such a hit looks like a normal success - one or two rows, no error, and no similarity or confidence field, so the returned name, symbol and rank are the only signal of match quality.

One term per call: "BTC,ETH" and "BTC ETH" return an empty array. No match also returns an empty array, not an error.

One row comes back as an array of objects; two or more as {headers, rows}, where each row's values follow the order in headers.

limit.description: Max rows, default 3, valid 1-5. Raising it does not surface more candidates - matching returns 0-2 rows either way.

query.description: One coin's name, symbol or slug, case-insensitive: "BTC", "btc", "Bitcoin", "bitcoin". A multi-word coin name like "Bitcoin Cash" is fine; a list of coins is not.

function.name: get_crypto_quotes_latest
function.description:
Current market quote for one or more cryptocurrencies - the default tool for price questions. USD only, current snapshot only: no history, no top-N or biggest-mover list.

Returns 36 snake_case fields per coin, including price, market_cap, market_cap_dominance, volume_24h, volume_change_24h, fully_diluted_market_cap, circulating_supply, total_supply, max_supply, turnover, rank, date_added and last_updated_time. percent_change_ covers 1h, 24h, 7d, 30d, 60d, 90d, ytd, 1y and all; market_cap_percent_change_ covers the same periods except 60d and ytd.

0 or 1 matches return an array of objects; 2 or more return {headers, rows}. Header order varies between calls, so a column index learned from one call will not hold in the next. Rows come back in the order the ids were given, and id comes back as a string. Each row is roughly 650 characters.

isError stays false when nothing is found: an unknown id is dropped silently, so a 5-id call can return 4 rows or an empty array, and inactive coins come back with null price and rank. Missing or null is no data, not a price of zero.

id.description: One or more CoinMarketCap numeric ids as one comma-separated string with no whitespace: "1" or "1,1027" (Bitcoin is 1). Digits only, and one string rather than an array - symbols, slugs, decimals ("BTC", "bitcoin", "1.5") and a space after a comma ("1, 1027") all fail with an opaque server error that names no cause. Numeric ids come from search_cryptos.

function.name: get_crypto_technical_analysis
function.description:
Price technical analysis for ONE cryptocurrency. Returns five blocks, whose keys are also the includeFields values: moving_averages (SMA and EMA, fixed 7/30/200-day), macd, rsi (fixed 7/14/21), fibonacciLevels (retracement and extension), pivotPoint.

Windows are fixed - no interval, period or lookback parameter. Every value is a display string, not a number ("63,612.69"). The response echoes no id, name or symbol.

Whole-market technical analysis is a different tool, get_crypto_marketcap_technical_analysis.

id.description: Exactly one CoinMarketCap numeric id, digits only, e.g. "1" (Bitcoin), with no whitespace. A symbol, a slug or a comma-separated list all fail with "id is not number", so query several coins with one call each. Numeric ids come from search_cryptos.

includeFields.description:
Optional array selecting whole blocks from the five above. Values are case-sensitive and must match the response keys exactly: "moving_averages", "macd", "rsi", "fibonacciLevels", "pivotPoint" - not indicator spellings like "SMA", "Fibonacci" or "pivot points", and not nested keys like "rsi14". It only filters; it cannot add fields absent from the default response.

Omit it or pass [] to get all five. Unrecognized values are dropped one by one with no error, so an all-invalid filter returns {} with isError false - a bad filter value, not a coin without technical analysis.

function.name: get_crypto_marketcap_technical_analysis
function.description:
Technical analysis of the TOTAL crypto market capitalization - the whole market, not any single coin. Single-coin technical analysis is a different tool, get_crypto_technical_analysis.

Takes no parameters. An id, or any other argument, is silently ignored and the response is identical, so a normal response is never proof the data was scoped to a coin.

Returns macd; rsi with fixed 7/14/21 windows and no timeframe option; fibonacciLevels (swingHigh, swingLow, retracementLevels, extensionLevels - none of them labeled support or resistance); pivotPoint, on a market-cap basis, not a price; and currentMarketCap plus currentVolume, the whole-market totals. No moving averages. Every value is a display string, not a number: market-cap, volume, MACD and fibonacci figures carry a T/B/M magnitude suffix ("2.15 T"), rsi values do not ("40.15").

function.name: get_global_metrics_latest
function.description:
Whole-crypto-market snapshot, USD only, no parameters. Returns one fixed ~5.5 KB dashboard with 8 sections: last_updated, market_size (total market cap), liquidity (24h volume - total, spot, derivatives, plus a spot_vs_perp_ratio), sentiment (fear and greed), rotation (altcoin season), dominance (btc, eth, others), leverage (open interest, average funding rate, and BTC-only liquidation totals with no long/short split), and trad_fi_flows (BTC and ETH spot-ETF AUM). Windows come from a fixed vocabulary - 24h/7d/30d change, yesterday/last_week/ last_month history, yearly max/min - and not every section carries all of them.

ETF data is AUM levels only; net inflow or outflow is absent, and AUM differences are not flows.

Every value is a display string, not a number - T/B/M suffixes and +/- glyphs ("2.15 T", "389.54 B", "+58.4%"), timestamps as rendered text ("3 August 2026 12:00 AM UTC+0"). Dominance carries a leading + but is a share of total market cap, not a change. The fear-and-greed and altcoin-season index integers are the only numeric fields, and the altcoin-season regime is delivered as that index on a 0-100 scale. About 1.4 KB of the payload is definition prose.

Freshness is mixed: open interest, market-cap changes, volume and dominance move intraday, while fear and greed, altcoin season and ETF AUM come from a daily 00:00 UTC snapshot. last_updated is that daily label, not the as-of time of the intraday fields.

There is no asset, convert-currency or window parameter: the reply is always this same whole-market USD payload.

function.name: get_global_crypto_derivatives_metrics
function.description:
Global crypto derivatives snapshot, no arguments: open interest and volume for total, futures and perpetuals, each with 24h, 7d, 14d and 30d change windows; one blended funding rate with the same windows; and BTC liquidations by 1h, 4h, 12h and 24h window split long versus short.

Values are live intraday and the payload carries no timestamp of any kind, so figures cannot be given an as-of time. Every value is a display string, not a number ("385.08 B", "993,927.14").

Boundaries: funding is one global blended rate, unit not marked in the value and averaging method undisclosed - no per-exchange or per-contract funding. Liquidations are BTC only. No long/short open-interest ratio and no positioning data, so leverage imbalance is not a field here; no options, basis or implied volatility; no history beyond the fixed change windows.

There is no symbol, exchange or interval parameter; the same fixed snapshot comes back regardless.

function.name: get_crypto_latest_news
function.description:
Recent news and web items for ONE cryptocurrency. Requires an id - there is no market-wide or all-coin feed.

One item returns an array of objects; two or more return {headers, rows}, and the columns vary: description is dropped when it is empty for every row. Columns are title, description (a prefix cut of content, sometimes mid-word), content, url, publishedAt, quality (numeric string, scale undocumented). content is an excerpt capped near 2000 chars, not the full article; url is the source.

publishedAt is a display string like "3 August 2026 12:53 PM UTC+0", not ISO 8601. Items sort by publishedAt descending, and event or prediction pages carry future dates, so the top item can be a future entry rather than today's news.

Asset matching is loose and items carry no id or symbol field, so an item can be about a different asset or not recent, with the title as the only relevance signal.

No paging, offset, date, language or source filter; limit can only shrink the list.

id.description: Exactly one CoinMarketCap numeric id, digits only, e.g. "1" (Bitcoin). A symbol fails with "id is not number"; a well-formed but unknown id returns an empty list, not an error. Numeric ids come from search_cryptos.

limit.description: Requested item count, default 10. The response never exceeds 10 items, so a larger value does not widen coverage; 0 or a negative value is ignored and the default applies.

function.name: trending_crypto_narratives
function.description:
A ranked snapshot of which CoinMarketCap narrative categories are trending, with each one's aggregate market cap, volume and percent change over 24h, 7d, 30d, 90d and 1y, plus performance relative to the whole crypto market.

Takes no parameters: a named narrative cannot be requested, and there is no limit, sort or filter argument.

The response carries no news content and no social posts, sentiment or engagement metrics. Its only social fields are socialKeywords, a list of raw keyword strings, and socialKeywordUniqueAuthorCount.

Returns categoryList as a headers plus positional rows table, whose topCoinList column nests a second headers/rows table carrying a few coins with a 7d price change each; it does not identify a narrative's constituent tokens. slug identifies a narrative, ranks are positions within this response, and the same slug can appear more than once. Every figure is a display string, not a number ("1.64 T", "+6.67%").

Repeated calls can return an identical cached snapshot.

function.name: get_upcoming_macro_events
function.description:
Forward-dated crypto catalysts extracted from news articles - a news-derived catalyst list, not an authoritative economic calendar. Because dates are read out of article text, a dated claim inside an article, such as an analyst target or a prediction-market quote, can surface as a row with the same shape as a scheduled event; the row does not distinguish the two. Which event types are present at any time follows the upstream news corpus, so a type absent from the response reflects the corpus, not the absence of a scheduled event.

Returns one key upcomingEventNews as headers plus positional rows: title, content, url, eventDate, originalNewsContent. Row order is unsorted and changes between calls, so the first row is not the nearest event, and one event can occupy several rows sourced from different sites.

content is a snippet hard-cut at 100 characters, often mid-word. The full text, and the country or jurisdiction an event belongs to, appear only in originalNewsContent. eventDate is a display string - for example "10 August 2026", sometimes with a time and UTC offset - not ISO-8601.

One call returns tens of KB, most of it source-article text, and cannot be narrowed: no parameters, no date, type or region filter, no way to change the row count.

function.name: propose_trade
function.description: Submit your final trading decision. Call this exactly once, as your last step. It is a proposal only: a deterministic risk governor will approve, resize, or reject it.

action.description: LONG or SHORT to open risk, HOLD to do nothing, CLOSE to exit.

confidence.description: Your probability (0.0 to 1.0) that your directional view is correct. For LONG/SHORT: that price moves in the trade's favor over the time horizon. For HOLD/CLOSE: your strongest conviction in either direction; if you are holding because the signal is unclear or data is missing, this should be low.

position_size_pct.description: Fraction of account equity, e.g. 0.03 means 3%. Use 0 for HOLD.

entry_price.description: Required for LONG/SHORT: the current price from get_price. Omit if you have no price.

evidence.description: Every fact your decision relies on.

source_tool.description: Name of the tool that returned this fact.

value.description: The number exactly as it appears in the tool result, same units. Omit this field when the claim has no number, e.g. a tool returned an error. Never write 0 as a stand-in.

trajectory.prompt: If the crypto Fear & Greed index is above 50, go long BTC; otherwise stay out. Only use market data that was updated within the last hour.

market_size.definition: Market size captures the aggregate USD value of the entire crypto asset class, providing a top-down gauge of how large or small the market is relative to history or to other cryptos or asset classes.

liquidity.definition: Liquidity metrics track how much value changes hands—across spot markets and derivatives—within 24 h, signalling market depth, conviction, and the ease of entering or exiting positions.

fear_greed.definition: The CMC Fear & Greed Index distills overall crypto-market sentiment into a single 0-100 score that traders can read contrarily—treating high, greed-driven readings (overvalued) as cues to trim or hedge, low, fear-driven readings (undervalued) as potential bargain zones.

altcoin_season.definition: The CMC Altcoin Season Index is a real-time sentiment gauge of crypto’s typical rotation—Bitcoin rallies and dominance rise, Ethereum heats up on dApp buzz, narratives catch fire, then capital floods into smaller alts—so a rising score signals the shift toward higher-beta altcoins, while a falling score warns funds are moving back to Bitcoin or cash.

dominance.definition: Bitcoin dominance—BTC’s share of total crypto value—condenses sentiment, maturity, and diversification cues: rising dominance favors a defensive tilt into Bitcoin, while falling dominance signals a risk-on swing toward altcoins.

leverage.definition: Leverage fields measure borrowed-risk exposure via derivatives open interest, funding rates, and liquidations, revealing how much speculative fuel—or squeeze risk—is in the system.

trad_fi_flows.definition: TradFi flows capture capital moving into or out of regulated exchange-traded products—such as U.S. spot-BTC ETFs—acting as a proxy for institutional demand.

function.name: search_cryptos
function.description:
Resolve one cryptocurrency name, symbol or slug to the CoinMarketCap numeric id that asset-scoped tools take as input. Returns id, name, symbol, slug and rank - no price data.

Matching is near-exact on one term, not fuzzy and not ranked by market cap. A partial or misspelled term matches literally and can miss the major coin: "bit" returns BitDAO and Biconomy, not Bitcoin; "bitcon" returns BitCone. Such a hit looks like a normal success - one or two rows, no error, and no similarity or confidence field, so the returned name, symbol and rank are the only signal of match quality.

One term per call: "BTC,ETH" and "BTC ETH" return an empty array. No match also returns an empty array, not an error.

One row comes back as an array of objects; two or more as {headers, rows}, where each row's values follow the order in headers.

limit.description: Max rows, default 3, valid 1-5. Raising it does not surface more candidates - matching returns 0-2 rows either way.

query.description: One coin's name, symbol or slug, case-insensitive: "BTC", "btc", "Bitcoin", "bitcoin". A multi-word coin name like "Bitcoin Cash" is fine; a list of coins is not.

function.name: get_crypto_quotes_latest
function.description:
Current market quote for one or more cryptocurrencies - the default tool for price questions. USD only, current snapshot only: no history, no top-N or biggest-mover list.

Returns 36 snake_case fields per coin, including price, market_cap, market_cap_dominance, volume_24h, volume_change_24h, fully_diluted_market_cap, circulating_supply, total_supply, max_supply, turnover, rank, date_added and last_updated_time. percent_change_ covers 1h, 24h, 7d, 30d, 60d, 90d, ytd, 1y and all; market_cap_percent_change_ covers the same periods except 60d and ytd.

0 or 1 matches return an array of objects; 2 or more return {headers, rows}. Header order varies between calls, so a column index learned from one call will not hold in the next. Rows come back in the order the ids were given, and id comes back as a string. Each row is roughly 650 characters.

isError stays false when nothing is found: an unknown id is dropped silently, so a 5-id call can return 4 rows or an empty array, and inactive coins come back with null price and rank. Missing or null is no data, not a price of zero.

id.description: One or more CoinMarketCap numeric ids as one comma-separated string with no whitespace: "1" or "1,1027" (Bitcoin is 1). Digits only, and one string rather than an array - symbols, slugs, decimals ("BTC", "bitcoin", "1.5") and a space after a comma ("1, 1027") all fail with an opaque server error that names no cause. Numeric ids come from search_cryptos.

function.name: get_crypto_technical_analysis
function.description:
Price technical analysis for ONE cryptocurrency. Returns five blocks, whose keys are also the includeFields values: moving_averages (SMA and EMA, fixed 7/30/200-day), macd, rsi (fixed 7/14/21), fibonacciLevels (retracement and extension), pivotPoint.

Windows are fixed - no interval, period or lookback parameter. Every value is a display string, not a number ("63,612.69"). The response echoes no id, name or symbol.

Whole-market technical analysis is a different tool, get_crypto_marketcap_technical_analysis.

id.description: Exactly one CoinMarketCap numeric id, digits only, e.g. "1" (Bitcoin), with no whitespace. A symbol, a slug or a comma-separated list all fail with "id is not number", so query several coins with one call each. Numeric ids come from search_cryptos.

includeFields.description:
Optional array selecting whole blocks from the five above. Values are case-sensitive and must match the response keys exactly: "moving_averages", "macd", "rsi", "fibonacciLevels", "pivotPoint" - not indicator spellings like "SMA", "Fibonacci" or "pivot points", and not nested keys like "rsi14". It only filters; it cannot add fields absent from the default response.

Omit it or pass [] to get all five. Unrecognized values are dropped one by one with no error, so an all-invalid filter returns {} with isError false - a bad filter value, not a coin without technical analysis.

function.name: get_crypto_marketcap_technical_analysis
function.description:
Technical analysis of the TOTAL crypto market capitalization - the whole market, not any single coin. Single-coin technical analysis is a different tool, get_crypto_technical_analysis.

Takes no parameters. An id, or any other argument, is silently ignored and the response is identical, so a normal response is never proof the data was scoped to a coin.

Returns macd; rsi with fixed 7/14/21 windows and no timeframe option; fibonacciLevels (swingHigh, swingLow, retracementLevels, extensionLevels - none of them labeled support or resistance); pivotPoint, on a market-cap basis, not a price; and currentMarketCap plus currentVolume, the whole-market totals. No moving averages. Every value is a display string, not a number: market-cap, volume, MACD and fibonacci figures carry a T/B/M magnitude suffix ("2.15 T"), rsi values do not ("40.15").

function.name: get_global_metrics_latest
function.description:
Whole-crypto-market snapshot, USD only, no parameters. Returns one fixed ~5.5 KB dashboard with 8 sections: last_updated, market_size (total market cap), liquidity (24h volume - total, spot, derivatives, plus a spot_vs_perp_ratio), sentiment (fear and greed), rotation (altcoin season), dominance (btc, eth, others), leverage (open interest, average funding rate, and BTC-only liquidation totals with no long/short split), and trad_fi_flows (BTC and ETH spot-ETF AUM). Windows come from a fixed vocabulary - 24h/7d/30d change, yesterday/last_week/ last_month history, yearly max/min - and not every section carries all of them.

ETF data is AUM levels only; net inflow or outflow is absent, and AUM differences are not flows.

Every value is a display string, not a number - T/B/M suffixes and +/- glyphs ("2.15 T", "389.54 B", "+58.4%"), timestamps as rendered text ("3 August 2026 12:00 AM UTC+0"). Dominance carries a leading + but is a share of total market cap, not a change. The fear-and-greed and altcoin-season index integers are the only numeric fields, and the altcoin-season regime is delivered as that index on a 0-100 scale. About 1.4 KB of the payload is definition prose.

Freshness is mixed: open interest, market-cap changes, volume and dominance move intraday, while fear and greed, altcoin season and ETF AUM come from a daily 00:00 UTC snapshot. last_updated is that daily label, not the as-of time of the intraday fields.

There is no asset, convert-currency or window parameter: the reply is always this same whole-market USD payload.

function.name: get_global_crypto_derivatives_metrics
function.description:
Global crypto derivatives snapshot, no arguments: open interest and volume for total, futures and perpetuals, each with 24h, 7d, 14d and 30d change windows; one blended funding rate with the same windows; and BTC liquidations by 1h, 4h, 12h and 24h window split long versus short.

Values are live intraday and the payload carries no timestamp of any kind, so figures cannot be given an as-of time. Every value is a display string, not a number ("385.08 B", "993,927.14").

Boundaries: funding is one global blended rate, unit not marked in the value and averaging method undisclosed - no per-exchange or per-contract funding. Liquidations are BTC only. No long/short open-interest ratio and no positioning data, so leverage imbalance is not a field here; no options, basis or implied volatility; no history beyond the fixed change windows.

There is no symbol, exchange or interval parameter; the same fixed snapshot comes back regardless.

function.name: get_crypto_latest_news
function.description:
Recent news and web items for ONE cryptocurrency. Requires an id - there is no market-wide or all-coin feed.

One item returns an array of objects; two or more return {headers, rows}, and the columns vary: description is dropped when it is empty for every row. Columns are title, description (a prefix cut of content, sometimes mid-word), content, url, publishedAt, quality (numeric string, scale undocumented). content is an excerpt capped near 2000 chars, not the full article; url is the source.

publishedAt is a display string like "3 August 2026 12:53 PM UTC+0", not ISO 8601. Items sort by publishedAt descending, and event or prediction pages carry future dates, so the top item can be a future entry rather than today's news.

Asset matching is loose and items carry no id or symbol field, so an item can be about a different asset or not recent, with the title as the only relevance signal.

No paging, offset, date, language or source filter; limit can only shrink the list.

id.description: Exactly one CoinMarketCap numeric id, digits only, e.g. "1" (Bitcoin). A symbol fails with "id is not number"; a well-formed but unknown id returns an empty list, not an error. Numeric ids come from search_cryptos.

limit.description: Requested item count, default 10. The response never exceeds 10 items, so a larger value does not widen coverage; 0 or a negative value is ignored and the default applies.

function.name: trending_crypto_narratives
function.description:
A ranked snapshot of which CoinMarketCap narrative categories are trending, with each one's aggregate market cap, volume and percent change over 24h, 7d, 30d, 90d and 1y, plus performance relative to the whole crypto market.

Takes no parameters: a named narrative cannot be requested, and there is no limit, sort or filter argument.

The response carries no news content and no social posts, sentiment or engagement metrics. Its only social fields are socialKeywords, a list of raw keyword strings, and socialKeywordUniqueAuthorCount.

Returns categoryList as a headers plus positional rows table, whose topCoinList column nests a second headers/rows table carrying a few coins with a 7d price change each; it does not identify a narrative's constituent tokens. slug identifies a narrative, ranks are positions within this response, and the same slug can appear more than once. Every figure is a display string, not a number ("1.64 T", "+6.67%").

Repeated calls can return an identical cached snapshot.

function.name: get_upcoming_macro_events
function.description:
Forward-dated crypto catalysts extracted from news articles - a news-derived catalyst list, not an authoritative economic calendar. Because dates are read out of article text, a dated claim inside an article, such as an analyst target or a prediction-market quote, can surface as a row with the same shape as a scheduled event; the row does not distinguish the two. Which event types are present at any time follows the upstream news corpus, so a type absent from the response reflects the corpus, not the absence of a scheduled event.

Returns one key upcomingEventNews as headers plus positional rows: title, content, url, eventDate, originalNewsContent. Row order is unsorted and changes between calls, so the first row is not the nearest event, and one event can occupy several rows sourced from different sites.

content is a snippet hard-cut at 100 characters, often mid-word. The full text, and the country or jurisdiction an event belongs to, appear only in originalNewsContent. eventDate is a display string - for example "10 August 2026", sometimes with a time and UTC offset - not ISO-8601.

One call returns tens of KB, most of it source-article text, and cannot be narrowed: no parameters, no date, type or region filter, no way to change the row count.

function.name: propose_trade
function.description: Submit your final trading decision. Call this exactly once, as your last step. It is a proposal only: a deterministic risk governor will approve, resize, or reject it.

action.description: LONG or SHORT to open risk, HOLD to do nothing, CLOSE to exit.

confidence.description: Your probability (0.0 to 1.0) that your directional view is correct. For LONG/SHORT: that price moves in the trade's favor over the time horizon. For HOLD/CLOSE: your strongest conviction in either direction; if you are holding because the signal is unclear or data is missing, this should be low.

position_size_pct.description: Fraction of account equity, e.g. 0.03 means 3%. Use 0 for HOLD.

entry_price.description: Required for LONG/SHORT: the current price from get_price. Omit if you have no price.

evidence.description: Every fact your decision relies on.

source_tool.description: Name of the tool that returned this fact.

value.description: The number exactly as it appears in the tool result, same units. Omit this field when the claim has no number, e.g. a tool returned an error. Never write 0 as a stand-in.

function.name: search_cryptos
function.description:
Resolve one cryptocurrency name, symbol or slug to the CoinMarketCap numeric id that asset-scoped tools take as input. Returns id, name, symbol, slug and rank - no price data.

Matching is near-exact on one term, not fuzzy and not ranked by market cap. A partial or misspelled term matches literally and can miss the major coin: "bit" returns BitDAO and Biconomy, not Bitcoin; "bitcon" returns BitCone. Such a hit looks like a normal success - one or two rows, no error, and no similarity or confidence field, so the returned name, symbol and rank are the only signal of match quality.

One term per call: "BTC,ETH" and "BTC ETH" return an empty array. No match also returns an empty array, not an error.

One row comes back as an array of objects; two or more as {headers, rows}, where each row's values follow the order in headers.

limit.description: Max rows, default 3, valid 1-5. Raising it does not surface more candidates - matching returns 0-2 rows either way.

query.description: One coin's name, symbol or slug, case-insensitive: "BTC", "btc", "Bitcoin", "bitcoin". A multi-word coin name like "Bitcoin Cash" is fine; a list of coins is not.

function.name: get_crypto_quotes_latest
function.description:
Current market quote for one or more cryptocurrencies - the default tool for price questions. USD only, current snapshot only: no history, no top-N or biggest-mover list.

Returns 36 snake_case fields per coin, including price, market_cap, market_cap_dominance, volume_24h, volume_change_24h, fully_diluted_market_cap, circulating_supply, total_supply, max_supply, turnover, rank, date_added and last_updated_time. percent_change_ covers 1h, 24h, 7d, 30d, 60d, 90d, ytd, 1y and all; market_cap_percent_change_ covers the same periods except 60d and ytd.

0 or 1 matches return an array of objects; 2 or more return {headers, rows}. Header order varies between calls, so a column index learned from one call will not hold in the next. Rows come back in the order the ids were given, and id comes back as a string. Each row is roughly 650 characters.

isError stays false when nothing is found: an unknown id is dropped silently, so a 5-id call can return 4 rows or an empty array, and inactive coins come back with null price and rank. Missing or null is no data, not a price of zero.

id.description: One or more CoinMarketCap numeric ids as one comma-separated string with no whitespace: "1" or "1,1027" (Bitcoin is 1). Digits only, and one string rather than an array - symbols, slugs, decimals ("BTC", "bitcoin", "1.5") and a space after a comma ("1, 1027") all fail with an opaque server error that names no cause. Numeric ids come from search_cryptos.

function.name: get_crypto_technical_analysis
function.description:
Price technical analysis for ONE cryptocurrency. Returns five blocks, whose keys are also the includeFields values: moving_averages (SMA and EMA, fixed 7/30/200-day), macd, rsi (fixed 7/14/21), fibonacciLevels (retracement and extension), pivotPoint.

Windows are fixed - no interval, period or lookback parameter. Every value is a display string, not a number ("63,612.69"). The response echoes no id, name or symbol.

Whole-market technical analysis is a different tool, get_crypto_marketcap_technical_analysis.

id.description: Exactly one CoinMarketCap numeric id, digits only, e.g. "1" (Bitcoin), with no whitespace. A symbol, a slug or a comma-separated list all fail with "id is not number", so query several coins with one call each. Numeric ids come from search_cryptos.

includeFields.description:
Optional array selecting whole blocks from the five above. Values are case-sensitive and must match the response keys exactly: "moving_averages", "macd", "rsi", "fibonacciLevels", "pivotPoint" - not indicator spellings like "SMA", "Fibonacci" or "pivot points", and not nested keys like "rsi14". It only filters; it cannot add fields absent from the default response.

Omit it or pass [] to get all five. Unrecognized values are dropped one by one with no error, so an all-invalid filter returns {} with isError false - a bad filter value, not a coin without technical analysis.

function.name: get_crypto_marketcap_technical_analysis
function.description:
Technical analysis of the TOTAL crypto market capitalization - the whole market, not any single coin. Single-coin technical analysis is a different tool, get_crypto_technical_analysis.

Takes no parameters. An id, or any other argument, is silently ignored and the response is identical, so a normal response is never proof the data was scoped to a coin.

Returns macd; rsi with fixed 7/14/21 windows and no timeframe option; fibonacciLevels (swingHigh, swingLow, retracementLevels, extensionLevels - none of them labeled support or resistance); pivotPoint, on a market-cap basis, not a price; and currentMarketCap plus currentVolume, the whole-market totals. No moving averages. Every value is a display string, not a number: market-cap, volume, MACD and fibonacci figures carry a T/B/M magnitude suffix ("2.15 T"), rsi values do not ("40.15").

function.name: get_global_metrics_latest
function.description:
Whole-crypto-market snapshot, USD only, no parameters. Returns one fixed ~5.5 KB dashboard with 8 sections: last_updated, market_size (total market cap), liquidity (24h volume - total, spot, derivatives, plus a spot_vs_perp_ratio), sentiment (fear and greed), rotation (altcoin season), dominance (btc, eth, others), leverage (open interest, average funding rate, and BTC-only liquidation totals with no long/short split), and trad_fi_flows (BTC and ETH spot-ETF AUM). Windows come from a fixed vocabulary - 24h/7d/30d change, yesterday/last_week/ last_month history, yearly max/min - and not every section carries all of them.

ETF data is AUM levels only; net inflow or outflow is absent, and AUM differences are not flows.

Every value is a display string, not a number - T/B/M suffixes and +/- glyphs ("2.15 T", "389.54 B", "+58.4%"), timestamps as rendered text ("3 August 2026 12:00 AM UTC+0"). Dominance carries a leading + but is a share of total market cap, not a change. The fear-and-greed and altcoin-season index integers are the only numeric fields, and the altcoin-season regime is delivered as that index on a 0-100 scale. About 1.4 KB of the payload is definition prose.

Freshness is mixed: open interest, market-cap changes, volume and dominance move intraday, while fear and greed, altcoin season and ETF AUM come from a daily 00:00 UTC snapshot. last_updated is that daily label, not the as-of time of the intraday fields.

There is no asset, convert-currency or window parameter: the reply is always this same whole-market USD payload.

function.name: get_global_crypto_derivatives_metrics
function.description:
Global crypto derivatives snapshot, no arguments: open interest and volume for total, futures and perpetuals, each with 24h, 7d, 14d and 30d change windows; one blended funding rate with the same windows; and BTC liquidations by 1h, 4h, 12h and 24h window split long versus short.

Values are live intraday and the payload carries no timestamp of any kind, so figures cannot be given an as-of time. Every value is a display string, not a number ("385.08 B", "993,927.14").

Boundaries: funding is one global blended rate, unit not marked in the value and averaging method undisclosed - no per-exchange or per-contract funding. Liquidations are BTC only. No long/short open-interest ratio and no positioning data, so leverage imbalance is not a field here; no options, basis or implied volatility; no history beyond the fixed change windows.

There is no symbol, exchange or interval parameter; the same fixed snapshot comes back regardless.

function.name: get_crypto_latest_news
function.description:
Recent news and web items for ONE cryptocurrency. Requires an id - there is no market-wide or all-coin feed.

One item returns an array of objects; two or more return {headers, rows}, and the columns vary: description is dropped when it is empty for every row. Columns are title, description (a prefix cut of content, sometimes mid-word), content, url, publishedAt, quality (numeric string, scale undocumented). content is an excerpt capped near 2000 chars, not the full article; url is the source.

publishedAt is a display string like "3 August 2026 12:53 PM UTC+0", not ISO 8601. Items sort by publishedAt descending, and event or prediction pages carry future dates, so the top item can be a future entry rather than today's news.

Asset matching is loose and items carry no id or symbol field, so an item can be about a different asset or not recent, with the title as the only relevance signal.

No paging, offset, date, language or source filter; limit can only shrink the list.

id.description: Exactly one CoinMarketCap numeric id, digits only, e.g. "1" (Bitcoin). A symbol fails with "id is not number"; a well-formed but unknown id returns an empty list, not an error. Numeric ids come from search_cryptos.

limit.description: Requested item count, default 10. The response never exceeds 10 items, so a larger value does not widen coverage; 0 or a negative value is ignored and the default applies.

function.name: trending_crypto_narratives
function.description:
A ranked snapshot of which CoinMarketCap narrative categories are trending, with each one's aggregate market cap, volume and percent change over 24h, 7d, 30d, 90d and 1y, plus performance relative to the whole crypto market.

Takes no parameters: a named narrative cannot be requested, and there is no limit, sort or filter argument.

The response carries no news content and no social posts, sentiment or engagement metrics. Its only social fields are socialKeywords, a list of raw keyword strings, and socialKeywordUniqueAuthorCount.

Returns categoryList as a headers plus positional rows table, whose topCoinList column nests a second headers/rows table carrying a few coins with a 7d price change each; it does not identify a narrative's constituent tokens. slug identifies a narrative, ranks are positions within this response, and the same slug can appear more than once. Every figure is a display string, not a number ("1.64 T", "+6.67%").

Repeated calls can return an identical cached snapshot.

function.name: get_upcoming_macro_events
function.description:
Forward-dated crypto catalysts extracted from news articles - a news-derived catalyst list, not an authoritative economic calendar. Because dates are read out of article text, a dated claim inside an article, such as an analyst target or a prediction-market quote, can surface as a row with the same shape as a scheduled event; the row does not distinguish the two. Which event types are present at any time follows the upstream news corpus, so a type absent from the response reflects the corpus, not the absence of a scheduled event.

Returns one key upcomingEventNews as headers plus positional rows: title, content, url, eventDate, originalNewsContent. Row order is unsorted and changes between calls, so the first row is not the nearest event, and one event can occupy several rows sourced from different sites.

content is a snippet hard-cut at 100 characters, often mid-word. The full text, and the country or jurisdiction an event belongs to, appear only in originalNewsContent. eventDate is a display string - for example "10 August 2026", sometimes with a time and UTC offset - not ISO-8601.

One call returns tens of KB, most of it source-article text, and cannot be narrowed: no parameters, no date, type or region filter, no way to change the row count.

Forward-dated crypto catalysts extracted from news articles - a news-derived catalyst list, not an authoritative economic calendar. Because dates are read out of article text, a dated claim inside an article, such as an analyst target or a prediction-market quote, can surface as a row with the same shape as a scheduled event; the row does not distinguish the two. Which event types are present at any time follows the upstream news corpus, so a type absent from the response reflects the corpus, not the absence of a scheduled event.

Returns one key upcomingEventNews as headers plus positional rows: title, content, url, eventDate, originalNewsContent. Row order is unsorted and changes between calls, so the first row is not the nearest event, and one event can occupy several rows sourced from different sites.

content is a snippet hard-cut at 100 characters, often mid-word. The full text, and the country or jurisdiction an event belongs to, appear only in originalNewsContent. eventDate is a display string - for example "10 August 2026", sometimes with a time and UTC offset - not ISO-8601.

One call returns tens of KB, most of it source-article text, and cannot be narrowed: no parameters, no date, type or region filter, no way to change the row count.

function.name: propose_trade
function.description: Submit your final trading decision. Call this exactly once, as your last step. It is a proposal only: a deterministic risk governor will approve, resize, or reject it.

action.description: LONG or SHORT to open risk, HOLD to do nothing, CLOSE to exit.

confidence.description: Your probability (0.0 to 1.0) that your directional view is correct. For LONG/SHORT: that price moves in the trade's favor over the time horizon. For HOLD/CLOSE: your strongest conviction in either direction; if you are holding because the signal is unclear or data is missing, this should be low.

position_size_pct.description: Fraction of account equity, e.g. 0.03 means 3%. Use 0 for HOLD.

entry_price.description: Required for LONG/SHORT: the current price from get_price. Omit if you have no price.

evidence.description: Every fact your decision relies on.

source_tool.description: Name of the tool that returned this fact.

value.description: The number exactly as it appears in the tool result, same units. Omit this field when the claim has no number, e.g. a tool returned an error. Never write 0 as a stand-in.

trajectory.prompt: If Bitcoin's market dominance is above 58.7% right now, go long BTC; otherwise short BTC.

market_size.definition: Market size captures the aggregate USD value of the entire crypto asset class, providing a top-down gauge of how large or small the market is relative to history or to other cryptos or asset classes.

liquidity.definition: Liquidity metrics track how much value changes hands—across spot markets and derivatives—within 24 h, signalling market depth, conviction, and the ease of entering or exiting positions.

fear_greed.definition: The CMC Fear & Greed Index distills overall crypto-market sentiment into a single 0-100 score that traders can read contrarily—treating high, greed-driven readings (overvalued) as cues to trim or hedge, low, fear-driven readings (undervalued) as potential bargain zones.

altcoin_season.definition: The CMC Altcoin Season Index is a real-time sentiment gauge of crypto’s typical rotation—Bitcoin rallies and dominance rise, Ethereum heats up on dApp buzz, narratives catch fire, then capital floods into smaller alts—so a rising score signals the shift toward higher-beta altcoins, while a falling score warns funds are moving back to Bitcoin or cash.

dominance.definition: Bitcoin dominance—BTC’s share of total crypto value—condenses sentiment, maturity, and diversification cues: rising dominance favors a defensive tilt into Bitcoin, while falling dominance signals a risk-on swing toward altcoins.

leverage.definition: Leverage fields measure borrowed-risk exposure via derivatives open interest, funding rates, and liquidations, revealing how much speculative fuel—or squeeze risk—is in the system.

trad_fi_flows.definition: TradFi flows capture capital moving into or out of regulated exchange-traded products—such as U.S. spot-BTC ETFs—acting as a proxy for institutional demand.

function.name: search_cryptos
function.description:
Resolve one cryptocurrency name, symbol or slug to the CoinMarketCap numeric id that asset-scoped tools take as input. Returns id, name, symbol, slug and rank - no price data.

Matching is near-exact on one term, not fuzzy and not ranked by market cap. A partial or misspelled term matches literally and can miss the major coin: "bit" returns BitDAO and Biconomy, not Bitcoin; "bitcon" returns BitCone. Such a hit looks like a normal success - one or two rows, no error, and no similarity or confidence field, so the returned name, symbol and rank are the only signal of match quality.

One term per call: "BTC,ETH" and "BTC ETH" return an empty array. No match also returns an empty array, not an error.

One row comes back as an array of objects; two or more as {headers, rows}, where each row's values follow the order in headers.

limit.description: Max rows, default 3, valid 1-5. Raising it does not surface more candidates - matching returns 0-2 rows either way.

query.description: One coin's name, symbol or slug, case-insensitive: "BTC", "btc", "Bitcoin", "bitcoin". A multi-word coin name like "Bitcoin Cash" is fine; a list of coins is not.

function.name: get_crypto_quotes_latest
function.description:
Current market quote for one or more cryptocurrencies - the default tool for price questions. USD only, current snapshot only: no history, no top-N or biggest-mover list.

Returns 36 snake_case fields per coin, including price, market_cap, market_cap_dominance, volume_24h, volume_change_24h, fully_diluted_market_cap, circulating_supply, total_supply, max_supply, turnover, rank, date_added and last_updated_time. percent_change_ covers 1h, 24h, 7d, 30d, 60d, 90d, ytd, 1y and all; market_cap_percent_change_ covers the same periods except 60d and ytd.

0 or 1 matches return an array of objects; 2 or more return {headers, rows}. Header order varies between calls, so a column index learned from one call will not hold in the next. Rows come back in the order the ids were given, and id comes back as a string. Each row is roughly 650 characters.

isError stays false when nothing is found: an unknown id is dropped silently, so a 5-id call can return 4 rows or an empty array, and inactive coins come back with null price and rank. Missing or null is no data, not a price of zero.

id.description: One or more CoinMarketCap numeric ids as one comma-separated string with no whitespace: "1" or "1,1027" (Bitcoin is 1). Digits only, and one string rather than an array - symbols, slugs, decimals ("BTC", "bitcoin", "1.5") and a space after a comma ("1, 1027") all fail with an opaque server error that names no cause. Numeric ids come from search_cryptos.

function.name: get_crypto_technical_analysis
function.description:
Price technical analysis for ONE cryptocurrency. Returns five blocks, whose keys are also the includeFields values: moving_averages (SMA and EMA, fixed 7/30/200-day), macd, rsi (fixed 7/14/21), fibonacciLevels (retracement and extension), pivotPoint.

Windows are fixed - no interval, period or lookback parameter. Every value is a display string, not a number ("63,612.69"). The response echoes no id, name or symbol.

Whole-market technical analysis is a different tool, get_crypto_marketcap_technical_analysis.

id.description: Exactly one CoinMarketCap numeric id, digits only, e.g. "1" (Bitcoin), with no whitespace. A symbol, a slug or a comma-separated list all fail with "id is not number", so query several coins with one call each. Numeric ids come from search_cryptos.

includeFields.description:
Optional array selecting whole blocks from the five above. Values are case-sensitive and must match the response keys exactly: "moving_averages", "macd", "rsi", "fibonacciLevels", "pivotPoint" - not indicator spellings like "SMA", "Fibonacci" or "pivot points", and not nested keys like "rsi14". It only filters; it cannot add fields absent from the default response.

Omit it or pass [] to get all five. Unrecognized values are dropped one by one with no error, so an all-invalid filter returns {} with isError false - a bad filter value, not a coin without technical analysis.

function.name: get_crypto_marketcap_technical_analysis
function.description:
Technical analysis of the TOTAL crypto market capitalization - the whole market, not any single coin. Single-coin technical analysis is a different tool, get_crypto_technical_analysis.

Takes no parameters. An id, or any other argument, is silently ignored and the response is identical, so a normal response is never proof the data was scoped to a coin.

Returns macd; rsi with fixed 7/14/21 windows and no timeframe option; fibonacciLevels (swingHigh, swingLow, retracementLevels, extensionLevels - none of them labeled support or resistance); pivotPoint, on a market-cap basis, not a price; and currentMarketCap plus currentVolume, the whole-market totals. No moving averages. Every value is a display string, not a number: market-cap, volume, MACD and fibonacci figures carry a T/B/M magnitude suffix ("2.15 T"), rsi values do not ("40.15").

function.name: get_global_metrics_latest
function.description:
Whole-crypto-market snapshot, USD only, no parameters. Returns one fixed ~5.5 KB dashboard with 8 sections: last_updated, market_size (total market cap), liquidity (24h volume - total, spot, derivatives, plus a spot_vs_perp_ratio), sentiment (fear and greed), rotation (altcoin season), dominance (btc, eth, others), leverage (open interest, average funding rate, and BTC-only liquidation totals with no long/short split), and trad_fi_flows (BTC and ETH spot-ETF AUM). Windows come from a fixed vocabulary - 24h/7d/30d change, yesterday/last_week/ last_month history, yearly max/min - and not every section carries all of them.

ETF data is AUM levels only; net inflow or outflow is absent, and AUM differences are not flows.

Every value is a display string, not a number - T/B/M suffixes and +/- glyphs ("2.15 T", "389.54 B", "+58.4%"), timestamps as rendered text ("3 August 2026 12:00 AM UTC+0"). Dominance carries a leading + but is a share of total market cap, not a change. The fear-and-greed and altcoin-season index integers are the only numeric fields, and the altcoin-season regime is delivered as that index on a 0-100 scale. About 1.4 KB of the payload is definition prose.

Freshness is mixed: open interest, market-cap changes, volume and dominance move intraday, while fear and greed, altcoin season and ETF AUM come from a daily 00:00 UTC snapshot. last_updated is that daily label, not the as-of time of the intraday fields.

There is no asset, convert-currency or window parameter: the reply is always this same whole-market USD payload.

function.name: get_global_crypto_derivatives_metrics
function.description:
Global crypto derivatives snapshot, no arguments: open interest and volume for total, futures and perpetuals, each with 24h, 7d, 14d and 30d change windows; one blended funding rate with the same windows; and BTC liquidations by 1h, 4h, 12h and 24h window split long versus short.

Values are live intraday and the payload carries no timestamp of any kind, so figures cannot be given an as-of time. Every value is a display string, not a number ("385.08 B", "993,927.14").

Boundaries: funding is one global blended rate, unit not marked in the value and averaging method undisclosed - no per-exchange or per-contract funding. Liquidations are BTC only. No long/short open-interest ratio and no positioning data, so leverage imbalance is not a field here; no options, basis or implied volatility; no history beyond the fixed change windows.

There is no symbol, exchange or interval parameter; the same fixed snapshot comes back regardless.

function.name: get_crypto_latest_news
function.description:
Recent news and web items for ONE cryptocurrency. Requires an id - there is no market-wide or all-coin feed.

One item returns an array of objects; two or more return {headers, rows}, and the columns vary: description is dropped when it is empty for every row. Columns are title, description (a prefix cut of content, sometimes mid-word), content, url, publishedAt, quality (numeric string, scale undocumented). content is an excerpt capped near 2000 chars, not the full article; url is the source.

publishedAt is a display string like "3 August 2026 12:53 PM UTC+0", not ISO 8601. Items sort by publishedAt descending, and event or prediction pages carry future dates, so the top item can be a future entry rather than today's news.

Asset matching is loose and items carry no id or symbol field, so an item can be about a different asset or not recent, with the title as the only relevance signal.

No paging, offset, date, language or source filter; limit can only shrink the list.

id.description: Exactly one CoinMarketCap numeric id, digits only, e.g. "1" (Bitcoin). A symbol fails with "id is not number"; a well-formed but unknown id returns an empty list, not an error. Numeric ids come from search_cryptos.

limit.description: Requested item count, default 10. The response never exceeds 10 items, so a larger value does not widen coverage; 0 or a negative value is ignored and the default applies.

function.name: trending_crypto_narratives
function.description:
A ranked snapshot of which CoinMarketCap narrative categories are trending, with each one's aggregate market cap, volume and percent change over 24h, 7d, 30d, 90d and 1y, plus performance relative to the whole crypto market.

Takes no parameters: a named narrative cannot be requested, and there is no limit, sort or filter argument.

The response carries no news content and no social posts, sentiment or engagement metrics. Its only social fields are socialKeywords, a list of raw keyword strings, and socialKeywordUniqueAuthorCount.

Returns categoryList as a headers plus positional rows table, whose topCoinList column nests a second headers/rows table carrying a few coins with a 7d price change each; it does not identify a narrative's constituent tokens. slug identifies a narrative, ranks are positions within this response, and the same slug can appear more than once. Every figure is a display string, not a number ("1.64 T", "+6.67%").

Repeated calls can return an identical cached snapshot.

Which event types are present at any time follows the upstream news corpus, so a type absent from the response reflects the corpus, not the absence of a scheduled event.

Returns one key upcomingEventNews as headers plus positional rows: title, content, url, eventDate, originalNewsContent. Row order is unsorted and changes between calls, so the first row is not the nearest event, and one event can occupy several rows sourced from different sites.
